risk_description: Offline data synchronization utilizing 'last-write-wins' strategy may result in data loss or state inconsistencies when a user modifies the same entity (e.g., ReadingSession) on multiple devices simultaneously or during prolonged offline periods.
root_cause: The reliance on simple client-side timestamping without server-side version vectors or conflict resolution logic creates race conditions during the batch processing of the sync queue.
mitigation_strategy: Implement a 'Sync Sequence Number' or version stamp on all entities. Reject updates with stale version numbers, forcing a client-side data refresh before re-queueing the mutation. Enforce atomic batch processing on the backend.
contingency_plan: Develop a conflict resolution UI on the mobile client to prompt users to choose the correct data version if an automatic merge fails.
monitoring_trigger: Backend logs showing > 5% of sync requests returning 409 Conflict status codes.

risk_description: The Google Books API proxy endpoint may hit upstream rate limits since all user traffic is funneled through a single backend IP address, potentially causing service outages for the book search feature.
root_cause: Architectural decision to proxy all search requests through the backend without a distributed IP strategy or sufficient aggressive caching layer.
mitigation_strategy: Implement aggressive Redis output caching for search queries (24-hour TTL for metadata). Implement a Token Bucket rate limiter per user IP on the backend proxy to prevent individual user abuse cascading to the upstream API.
contingency_plan: Activate 'Manual Entry Only' mode on the mobile client via Feature Flag if the Search API health check fails consistently.
monitoring_trigger: Polly Circuit Breaker entering 'Open' state for the Google Books Service more than 3 times in one hour.

risk_description: AI Recommendation engine costs may exceed budget projections due to the high computational cost of generating embeddings and GPT-4 inference calls, especially if the 5/month limit for Free users is bypassed or inefficiently enforced.
root_cause: Lack of strict cost-control gates at the API level and potential for 'prompt injection' or abuse if the API endpoint is not strictly validated against the user's subscription tier claims.
mitigation_strategy: Implement strict server-side validation of the 'https://readtrack.com/roles' claim before invoking OpenAI. Cache RAG responses based on user history hash to avoid re-generating recommendations for unchanged data.
contingency_plan: Downgrade the inference model from GPT-4 to GPT-3.5-Turbo or disable the feature for Free tier users entirely via remote configuration.
monitoring_trigger: OpenAI API daily spend exceeds 80% of the allocated budget threshold set in AWS Cost Anomaly Detection.

risk_description: Aurora Serverless v2 'cold start' latency may violate the <200ms P95 requirement if the database auto-pauses during periods of low traffic (e.g., development or initial rollout phase).
root_cause: Configuration of Aurora Serverless v2 with a Minimum ACU (Aurora Capacity Unit) of 0 (auto-pause) to save costs in non-production environments, potentially bleeding into production config.
mitigation_strategy: Enforce Minimum ACU of 0.5 in the Production CDK stack context to prevent auto-pausing. Implement synthetic canary transactions to keep the database warm during off-peak hours.
contingency_plan: Switch to provisioned RDS instances if Serverless v2 scaling latency proves inconsistent for the application's specific read/write patterns.
monitoring_trigger: CloudWatch Alarms for 'ServerlessDatabaseCapacity' dropping to 0 or API Latency P95 exceeding 300ms.

risk_description: Isar local database schema changes in future updates may cause mobile app crashes or data corruption if migration logic is not strictly versioned and tested on existing datasets.
root_cause: Mobile apps require client-side migration scripts that run on the user's device. Changing Isar collection structures without a robust migration strategy leads to incompatible local files.
mitigation_strategy: Establish a strict 'Schema Versioning Protocol'. All schema changes must include a corresponding migration script tested against a prepopulated database from the previous version.
contingency_plan: Implement a 'Safe Mode' that detects database corruption on startup, wipes the local cache, and forces a full re-sync from the backend.
monitoring_trigger: Crashlytics reports showing 'IsarError' or schema mismatch exceptions increasing after a release.

risk_description: Failure to achieve GDPR compliance regarding 'Right to Erasure' due to data fragmentation across Aurora, OpenSearch, and S3, leading to potential legal liability.
root_cause: Data is replicated across the transactional DB, the search index, and potentially the embedding vector store. A delete command might verify against the DB but fail to propagate to the async search index.
mitigation_strategy: Implement a 'User Deleted' distributed domain event. Create a dedicated 'Deletion Verification Job' that queries all data stores (SQL, NoSQL, Vector) 24 hours after deletion to certify data removal.
contingency_plan: Manual deletion runbooks for Ops team to scrub data from OpenSearch and S3 upon audit failure.
monitoring_trigger: Audit log reconciliation alert showing mismatch between 'Delete Requests' and 'Deletion Confirmations'.
